lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
Date of birth: 21 Jul 1998 | Nationality: Indian
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator that tightens the previous bound by a log factor; it is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability and writes the problem sets, earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Pioneered a data-driven, research-first approach to volatility modeling that delivered robust, actionable insights.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch
Methods: time-series econometrics, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: The résumé includes personal details that are conventionally left off.
items.because: Date of birth and nationality can distract from the candidate’s qualifications.

items.says: The Northpeak and Kaggle bullets appear to describe the same order-book imbalance result with different dates and framing.
items.because: Both report a 0.4 Sharpe increase over 18 months, leaving it unclear whether they are separate results.

items.says: The dates leave an eight-month gap between the B.S. and the Research Assistant role.
“Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35%” lacks a return measure, comparison point and period.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the 35% represents or how to interpret it.

items.says: Purged splits and an embargo do not guarantee that every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: They do not verify the full data and feature pipeline, so other look-ahead can remain.

items.says: The point-in-time explanation is lengthy without stating a separate validation result.
items.because: It leaves the outcome of testing six years of data unstated.

items.says: “Validated the signal” does not state the validation result.
items.because: A reader can see how the signal was tested, but not what the test established.

items.says: The feature-store reuse outcome is delayed by a bulky relative clause.
The live-allocation outcome is delayed until after the presentation details.
The best Sharpe from 400 backtested configurations is not a valid estimate of expected live Sharpe as written.
items.because: Selecting the best configuration tends to select for backtest noise and upward-bias its Sharpe.

items.says: The line gives neither the best Sharpe value nor a clear basis for calling it a live estimate.
items.because: A reader cannot distinguish a measured backtest figure from a live-performance expectation.

items.says: The Sharpe improvement is buried after the signal description and evaluation details.
items.because: A reader scanning the entry may miss its clearest result.

items.says: “Desk book” is team-specific jargon that may not be clear to outside readers.
Using the same random seed on every worker can invalidate the Monte Carlo study.
items.because: Workers can produce identical or overlapping random streams and undermine simulation independence.

items.says: “By running the runs in parallel” repeats “runs” and makes the method cumbersome.
The comparison for the claimed log-factor improvement is unidentified.
items.because: A reader cannot tell which prior result the bound improves on or whether the comparison depends on a particular regime.

items.says: The variance-bound contribution should lead the Research Assistant entry.
items.because: It is the entry’s clearest research contribution.

items.says: The paper-status clause makes the sentence less direct.
“Taught … and writes” mixes past and present tense in a completed role.
items.because: “Writes” makes the problem-set work sound current despite the role’s 2021 end date.

items.says: The 4.8/5 teaching rating lacks its source and response count.
items.because: A reader cannot judge how the rating was gathered or how representative it is.

items.says: The opening claim is vague and does not connect its claimed impact to the study’s concrete research sequence.
items.because: “Robust, actionable insights” does not say what changed or how anyone used the result.

items.says: The opening does not identify the modeling approach used.
items.because: “Data-driven” and “research-first” provide little technical evidence about the study.

items.says: The significance result does not define the forecast gain, its size or the benchmark.
items.because: Statistical significance alone does not show the practical value of the improvement.

items.says: The 24-index result is buried after the test and correction.
items.because: The main finding arrives late for a reader scanning the bullet.

items.says: “The 30 indices” includes an unnecessary article.
“Which was presented” leaves unclear who presented the paper.
The competition entry gives no result from the feature-engineering and modeling work.
items.because: Without a placement or score relative to the field, the contribution is difficult to assess.

items.says: The 0.02 gap has no named score metric or scale.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the difference measures or whether it is large.

items.says: The most concrete competition outcome appears last in the entry.
items.because: A reader has to reach the final bullet to find its clearest measurable outcome.

items.says: “Tested over 18 months out of sample” has an unclear referent.
